setup.zh: 娘把最后一点白面烙成两张饼，厚的给你；爹拿麻布缠紧了膝盖。娘说：打得过就打，打不过就跑。
setup.en: Mother bakes the last of the white flour into two flatbreads, the thick one for you; Father binds his knee tight. Mother says: fight if you can win; if not, run.

recap.zh: 娘把最后一点白面烙成饼塞给你：「打不过就跑——跑不丢人。」
recap.en: Mother gave you bread from the last of the flour: "If you can't win, run — there's no shame in running."

zh: 灶间亮了灯。最后一点白面，烙成两张饼。
en: A lamp in the kitchen. The last of the flour, baked into two breads.

story.zh:
他关上窗，一回身，灶间的灯已经亮了，他娘蹲在灶前烙饼，烙的竟是白面的。家里那只装白面的小布袋，小满知道，已经瘪了一个月了。

他娘把最后一点面全抖了出来，抖了三遍，连布袋缝里的面粉都拍了个干净，烙成了两张饼，一张厚，一张薄。

他爹坐在炕沿上，拿一块旧麻布一圈一圈地缠他的左膝，缠完了站起身来，试着走了两步，脸上的肉抽了一下，又若无其事地坐了回去，冲小满咧嘴一笑，道：「没事。老毛病。它今天话有点多。」

他娘没回头，问道：「他爹，你真要去黑松岭？」他爹道：「前山叫马家篦空了，不去不行。」他娘道：「你那腿——」他爹道：「我这腿是不行了。」顿了一顿，又道：「还有孩子的腿。」

他娘手里的铲子停了一下。跟着她把那张厚的饼铲了出来，拿一块干净的布包好，走过来塞进小满怀里；薄的那张，给了他爹；她自己一张也没有。

她蹲下来，看着小满的眼睛，声音压得极低，低得只有他们两个听得见：「你爹老实。一辈子不会算计人，也不会防着人。你不一样。你随我。」

说着伸手掐掉了他衣襟上的一根线头，又道：「山里的东西，比马三还狠。遇事，先想，再动。想明白了，打得过就打，打不过就跑。跑，不丢人。」

小满道：「嗯。」他娘道：「还有。昨天那一下，娘看见了。」小满抬起头来。他娘道：「你没还手。对的。」她的嘴角极轻极轻地动了一下，又道：「你回的那句嘴——也对。」她伸手把他额前的头发拢了拢，道：「可也别忘了。」

他爹在身后咳了两声，背起了那张弓。他娘站在门口——门口其实没有门，门还在阿禾家的菜地里——看着一大一小两个背影，走进天边那一线灰白里去。她没有喊，也没有挥手，就那么一直站着，直站到小满回头也看不见她了。
story.en:
He shut the window and turned round: the lamp in the kitchen was already lit, and his mother was crouched at the stove making flatbread — of white flour, no less. The little cloth bag that held the white flour, Xiaoman knew, had been flat for a month.

His mother shook out the very last of the flour, shook it three times, slapped even the dust from the bag's seams, and made two flatbreads, one thick, one thin.

His father sat on the edge of the kang binding his left knee round and round with an old strip of hemp. Done, he stood, tried a couple of steps, and a muscle in his face twitched; then he sat back down as if nothing had happened and grinned at Xiaoman. "It's nothing. Old trouble. It's a bit talkative today."

His mother didn't turn round. "You're really going to Black Pine Ridge?" His father said, "The Ma family has combed the front hills bare. There's nothing for it." His mother said, "Your leg —" His father said, "The leg's no good." A pause. "There's the boy's legs too."

The spatula in his mother's hand stopped for a moment. Then she lifted out the thick flatbread, wrapped it in a clean cloth, came over and tucked it inside Xiaoman's jacket; the thin one she gave his father; for herself there was none.

She crouched and looked him in the eye, her voice pitched so low only the two of them could hear: "Your father's honest. All his life he's never schemed against anyone, nor guarded against anyone. You're different. You take after me." She pinched a loose thread off his jacket front.

"The things in the mountains are fiercer than Ma San. When something happens, think first, then move. Once you've thought it through — if you can win, fight; if you can't, run. Running's no shame."

Xiaoman said, "Mm." His mother paused. "And. That shove yesterday — I saw it." Xiaoman looked up. His mother said, "You didn't hit back. That was right." The corner of her mouth moved very, very slightly. "What you said back — that was right too." She smoothed the hair off his forehead. "But don't forget it either."

His father coughed twice behind him and shouldered the bow. His mother stood in the doorway — there was no door in the doorway, in fact; the door was still in Ahe's family's plot — watching the two backs, one big, one small, walk off into the thin grey line at the edge of the sky. She didn't call out, and she didn't wave; she just stood there, until Xiaoman, turning back, could no longer see her.

exits.means: sets off with father into the mountain, moves on
